best.note: a_limit/t_fire manually pinned to the original documented values (60.0C, ~3% frame) -- empirically INERT across their whole tested range at t_ign=41.5 (see the tied rows in this grid), so calibration provides no evidence to move them; only t_ign is load-bearing on this corpus.

selection_methodology: Restricted to precision>=0.8, then ranked by F1 (see calibrate_otsu_thresholds.py --min-precision). The UNCONSTRAINED F1-best (no precision floor) is recorded below as rejected_degenerate_f1_optimum: it predicts fire on nearly every frame (recall~98%, precision~28%, accuracy~29%) because F1 never penalizes false positives via tn -- operationally useless for a safety system despite a nontrivially higher raw F1 score.

held_out_comparison.note: Both measured on the real stateful OtsuFireDetector (session-level temporal continuity via evaluate_fire_timed), held out on fire_test_scenes -- NOT the stateless per-frame grid-search proxy above, which understates recall since it cannot benefit from Stage-3 temporal-growth persistence within a session (reset() before every frame). Calibration recovered +12.3pp F1 and +12.3pp recall for -17pp precision (100%->83%, i.e. 45 new false alarms out of 1334 negative frames, ~3.4% false-alarm rate) -- a real, positive result, not just confirmation that the untested guess was already fine.
